title: Two-fibre products of arbitrary groupoid stacks are stacks
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and a site $(\mathcal C,J)$ [def-weil-pbc-topos] small in the larger universe. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal D$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C$, with fibre groupoids in that universe: pullback objects exist along every base arrow, with the cartesian unique factorization property, and every fibre is a groupoid. Assume they are $J$-stacks, meaning that their isomorphism presheaves on slice sites are sheaves and all descent data on covering sieves are effective. Let $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ and $v:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ be pullback-compatible functors over $\mathcal C$. Form the category $\mathcal Q$ over $\mathcal C$ whose objects over $T$ are triples $(a,b,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$, $b\in\mathcal B(T)$ and $\alpha:u(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}v(b)$; its vertical arrows $(a,b,\alpha)\to(a',b',\alpha')$ are pairs $(s:a\to a',t:b\to b')$ with $v(t)\alpha=\alpha'u(s)$, and its pullbacks are induced from those of the three factors. Then $\mathcal Q$ is a $J$-stack in groupoids. Its two projections and tautological isomorphism $u\operatorname{pr}_1\cong v\operatorname{pr}_2$ give a two-fibre product of $\mathcal A\to\mathcal D\leftarrow\mathcal B$ in the 2-category of $J$-stacks, pullback-compatible functors and natural isomorphisms over the identity of the base.

source.place: Tags 026G (lemma-2-product-stacks) and 02ZL (lemma-2-product-stacks-in-groupoids); the covering-sieve formulation uses exactly the same gluing argument and requires no fibre products in the base.

proof.text: Use the larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention]; all triples and arrow pairs below form sets in it. Complete the description of $\mathcal Q$ by taking an arrow over $f:T'\to T$ to be a pair $(s:a'\to a,t:b'\to b)$ over $f$ satisfying $v(t)\alpha'=\alpha u(s)$. Identities and composition are componentwise: if also $v(t')\alpha''=\alpha'u(s')$, then $v(tt')\alpha''=\alpha u(ss')$. Thus the equation is preserved by composition. For a vertical arrow its inverse pair satisfies $v(t^{-1})\alpha=\alpha'u(s^{-1})$, obtained by multiplying its equation by the inverses. Hence each fibre is a groupoid, and the component projections are functors over $\mathcal C$.

For $q=(a,b,\alpha)$ over $T$ and $f:T'\to T$, choose cartesian lifts $r:a_f\to a$ and $s:b_f\to b$. Since $u(r)$ and $v(s)$ are cartesian, factor $\alpha u(r)$ uniquely through $v(s)$ to obtain a vertical $\alpha_f:u(a_f)\to v(b_f)$. It is invertible because the fibre of $\mathcal D$ is a groupoid. Then $(r,s):(a_f,b_f,\alpha_f)\to q$ is cartesian: given $(r',s')$ over $fh$, factor its components uniquely as $rr''$ and $ss''$ over $h$; cancelling the cartesian arrow $v(s)$ in $v(s)v(s'')\alpha'=\alpha u(r)u(r'')$ gives $v(s'')\alpha'=\alpha_f u(r'')$. This proves existence and uniqueness of the factorization in $\mathcal Q$. Identity and composite pullback comparisons are the unique vertical maps commuting with the lifts, so satisfy their coherence equations by uniqueness. Projections preserve these lifts. The arrow equation makes the components $\alpha$ a natural isomorphism $u\operatorname{pr}_1\cong v\operatorname{pr}_2$.

source.place: Tag 02XQ (lemma-2-product-fibred-categories-over-C), with the omitted cartesian-factorization check supplied.

proof.text: For $q=(a,b,\alpha)$ and $q'=(a',b',\alpha')$ over $T$, an isomorphism after restriction to $W\to T$ is precisely a pair $(s,t)$ in $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal A}(a,a')(W)\times\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal B}(b,b')(W)$ with $v(t)\alpha=\alpha'u(s)$, using the pullback comparisons of step 2. Given a matching family of such pairs on a covering sieve of $W$, glue $s$ and $t$ uniquely by the two factor sheaf hypotheses and the matching-family definition in [def-weil-pbc-topos]. The two sides of the equation are sections of the sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal D}(u(a),v(b'))$ restricted to $W$; they agree on the covering sieve, hence agree on $W$ by uniqueness in that sheaf. The glued pair therefore lies in $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Q}(q,q')$, and uniqueness follows componentwise. This proves its sheaf condition on every slice without any assumption about fibre products in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 026G (lemma-2-product-stacks), morphism-presheaf paragraph, expressed directly by matching families.

proof.text:
Let $R\in J(T)$ and let a descent datum in $\mathcal Q$ be given on $R$. Write its objects as $q_f=(a_f,b_f,\alpha_f)$ for $f:W\to T$ in $R$. For $h:V\to W$, write its transition vertically as $(s_h,t_h):h^*q_f\to q_{fh}$. Thus $v(t_h)h^*\alpha_f=\alpha_{fh}u(s_h)$. Projecting the identity and composition equations gives descent data in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$. Their effectiveness, assumed in the statement, supplies $a,b$ over $T$ and compatible vertical isomorphisms $e_f:f^*a\to a_f$, $d_f:f^*b\to b_f$. Put $\gamma_f=v(d_f)^{-1}\alpha_f u(e_f)$, a section over $f$ of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal D}(u(a),v(b))$, using the canonical pullback comparisons of $u,v$. Compatibility says $e_{fh}=s_h h^*e_f$ and $d_{fh}=t_h h^*d_f$, after the unique composite-pullback identifications of step 2. Hence
$$\gamma_{fh}=v(h^*d_f)^{-1}v(t_h)^{-1}\alpha_{fh}u(s_h)u(h^*e_f)=v(h^*d_f)^{-1}h^*\alpha_f u(h^*e_f)=h^*\gamma_f.$$
This is a matching family on the covering sieve, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-topos].

source.place: Tag 026G (lemma-2-product-stacks), descent paragraph, with covering-sieve transitions and conjugation written explicitly.

proof.text: The $\mathcal D$-sheaf hypothesis and [def-weil-pbc-topos] glue the matching family $\gamma_f$ uniquely to an isomorphism $\alpha:u(a)\to v(b)$. Set $q=(a,b,\alpha)$. By the formula for $\gamma_f=f^*\alpha$, one has $v(d_f)f^*\alpha=\alpha_f u(e_f)$, so $(e_f,d_f):f^*q\to q_f$ is an arrow of $\mathcal Q$, not merely a pair of arrows in the factors. It is invertible by step 1. Its compatibility with each transition is precisely the two compatibility equations for $e_f,d_f$ used in step 4; equality of pairs is equality of their components. Thus these arrows identify the given descent datum with that of $q$. Together with steps 2 and 3, this proves that $\mathcal Q$ is a stack in groupoids. The argument also applies to an empty covering sieve: effectiveness in the two factors supplies $a,b$, and the empty matching family has its unique amalgamation in the $\mathcal D$-isomorphism sheaf.

source.place: Tags 026G (lemma-2-product-stacks), including its omitted final descent verification, and 02ZL (lemma-2-product-stacks-in-groupoids).

proof.text: For any $J$-stack $\mathcal W$ and pullback-compatible $F:\mathcal W\to\mathcal A$, $G:\mathcal W\to\mathcal B$ with natural isomorphism $\theta:uF\cong vG$ over the base, define $H(w)=(F(w),G(w),\theta_w)$ and $H(k)=(F(k),G(k))$. Naturality of $\theta$ is exactly the arrow equation, so this is a functor; its identity and composition laws are those of $F,G$. The componentwise cartesian-factorization argument in step 2 shows that pairs of cartesian arrows are cartesian in $\mathcal Q$; therefore $H$ preserves pullbacks. Conversely, projecting any pullback-compatible $H$ gives $F,G$ and pulling back the tautological isomorphism gives $\theta$. These constructions recover the object and arrow assignments exactly.

source.place: Tag 0040 (lemma-2-product-categories-over-C), universal functor, restricted to pullback-compatible functors.

proof.text: Between cone data $(F,G,\theta)$ and $(F',G',\theta')$, a morphism is a pair of natural isomorphisms $\sigma:F\cong F'$, $\tau:G\cong G'$ over the base with $v(\tau)\theta=\theta'u(\sigma)$. Its components $(\sigma_w,\tau_w)$ are exactly the components of a natural isomorphism $H\cong H'$ in $\mathcal Q$; naturality follows in each component, and conversely follows by projection. This correspondence is bijective, and respects identities and composition because these are componentwise. Hence the groupoid of functors $\mathcal W\to\mathcal Q$ and base-preserving natural isomorphisms is isomorphic to the groupoid of these cones. Precomposition acts on both descriptions by the same component formulas. This is the required 2-fibre-product universal property in $J$-stacks.
